title: Alphabet's Waymo secures $5 billion term loan to accelerate expansion
source_used: TechCrunch (Reuters, the item's outlet, is behind a login)
key_facts: Waymo, Alphabet's self-driving car unit, closed a $5 billion loan, its first debt financing.
Lenders include PIMCO, Blackstone, Sixth Street, Apollo, Fidelity and others; Goldman Sachs was sole lead bookrunner.
Waymo announced it on Thursday 8 Oct 2026.
In February 2026 Waymo raised $16 billion in equity at a $126 billion valuation; Alphabet remains majority investor.
Waymo offers robotaxi service in 15 markets and is testing in London and Tokyo.
Waymo calls the loan a step in becoming a 'scaling commercial enterprise'.
US safety regulators (NHTSA, NTSB) have open investigations into Waymo vehicles around school buses and a child struck at about 6 mph.
quote_evidence: Waymo, the autonomous vehicle technology company under Google parent Alphabet, closed a $5 billion loan from a series of high-profile lenders, including PIMCO, Blackstone, and Sixth Street.
Waymo now offers robotaxi services in 15 markets.
The company’s growth has also spurred criticism and increased attention from regulators.
why_it_matters_hint: Gives the leading US robotaxi operator new money to expand beyond its parent and equity investors.
